transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Morales (CISO - Argent Labs), Sofia Ruiz (Security Engineer), Daniel Park (Procurement)
Shared artifacts: Trust Center link (https://redwood.example.com/trust-center/argent-labs), SOC 2 Type II PDF (shared), ISO controls matrix (will be shared)

Summary: Quick posture review of Redwood's SOC 2 and ISO 27001 artifacts, questions on RBAC/SSO, audit log retention and exports, KMS/encryption key custody, and data residency for EU workloads. Goal: decide whether to proceed with Trust Center access and a technical KMS deep dive next week.

Topics: SOC 2 scope and date, ISO 27001 mapping, trust center access, RBAC / SSO integration (SAML / SCIM), audit logs and retention, encryption (KMS/HSM) key custody, data residency requirements, Dedicated vs Private deployment controls

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this deal. With me is Priya, our security and infra SE.
[00:06] Evan Morales: Thanks Jordan. We got about 45 minutes. Main thing for us is to see where Redwood stands on SOC 2 / ISO artifacts and KMS. We've got a list from procurement and security.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Hi all. Quick agenda: I'll run through the SOC 2 scope and our Trust Center, then we can dig into RBAC/SSO and KMS. Sound good?
[00:21] Sofia Ruiz: Yeah that's perfect. We scrolled the deck you sent but want confirma-- confirmation on E2E encryption and whether Redwood holds customer KEYS or if we can provide our own.
[00:31] Jordan Lee: Totally. We'll go through the options. Quick note: we host attestation artifacts in the Trust Center, link is in the calendar. We can give view-only creds to Evan or your security folks.
[00:40] Daniel Park: For procurement, we need the SOC 2 Type II dates and the auditor name-- also the ISO cert scope, is it global?
[00:47] Priya Nair: SOC 2 Type II report is for the period Jan 2025 - Dec 2025, auditor is Kearns & Boyle (phonetic in transcript, may be spelled differently in the report). ISO 27001 certification covers our control plane and hosted API regions, not customer-managed on-prem packages. We'll attach the ISO summary.
[01:05] Evan Morales: Ok, good. Data residency: Argent Labs requires EU-only data residency for certain customer segments. How do you enforce region controls and what evidence can you provide?
[01:14] Priya Nair: We have region binding for hosted API--requests can be routed to EU clusters and logs/audit exports respect region. For Dedicated/Private you can pin to a VPC region. Evidence we provide: invoices and infra region tags plus our controls map in Trust Center. We'll add an EU residency attestation snapshot for you.
[01:30] Sofia Ruiz: About RBAC and SSO: we use Okta; we need SAML2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning, and fine-grained role controls for admins vs ops. Can Redwood integrate and support least privilege?
[01:42] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is role-based with built-in roles and custom roles. There's API for role assignment and audit trail on all role changes. Note: some smaller features on the console still use legacy labels -- the audit trail is full but the UI label might be slightly different.
[01:58] Jordan Lee: Also worth noting, for Private deployments we can enable customer-managed SSO endpoints via your IdP.
[02:05] Evan Morales: Audit logs: retention and export capabilities? We need at least two years of tamper-evident audit logs for compliance. How do you ensure immutability?
[02:16] Priya Nair: We retain admin audit logs for 2 years by default in the hosted plan and 7 years in Dedicated with an add-on. Logs are written to append-only storage with signed manifests; for Private you can configure export to your SIEM or S3 with bucket policies and object lock to achieve WORM-like behavior. We'll include implementation details in the Trust Center doc.
[02:40] Sofia Ruiz: Great, can you show how to pull a filtered export -- say all role changes for last quarter?
[02:46] Priya Nair: We'll schedule the technical deep dive but briefly: there's an admin API with filters (actor, event type, date range) and a one-click export from the console that generates NDJSON. Sometimes the console label calls it "audit dump" which is a bit rough, but it works.
[03:02] Daniel Park: On encryption: who holds the keys? We need to know if Redwood ever has plaintext access.
[03:09] Priya Nair: By default, Redwood uses provider KMS (cloud KMS) for server-side encryption; we manage keys when you use Hosted. For Dedicated or Private you can bring your own KMS keys via key import or HSM (we support AWS KMS and external HSM via KMIP in Private). We do have access to key metadata but not plaintext keys when you provide your own. For strict control, we support envelope encryption with customer KMS so root key stays in customer control.
[03:34] Evan Morales: You said KMIP for HSM -- can you give more details? Who maintains the HSM and what's the network setup?
[03:40] Priya Nair: For Private deployments, customers can deploy an on-prem HSM or managed cloud HSM. We connect over mutual TLS, and Redwood's control plane stores only wrapped keys and references. We can provide architecture diagrams; will include a network diagram in the follow-up.
[03:54] Jordan Lee: Quick interjection--some of the vendor names in the doc are spelled slightly different; the auditor name in the PDF is Kearns & Boyle, spelled K-E-A-R-N-S in the report, I think that fixeds the earlier phonetic.
[04:05] Evan Morales: Thanks. A couple of compliance questions: does Redwood provide a bridge of controls mapping from SOC2 to ISO 27001 so we can ingest into our compliance tooling?
[04:13] Priya Nair: Yes, we have a controls mapping matrix; I'll export a mapping (SOC 2 CC/PII -> ISO 27001 Annex A controls) and send it. We'll mark which controls are in scope for hosted, dedicated, and private.
[04:26] Sofia Ruiz: On trust center access -- will we get raw artifacts (full SOC 2 PDF) or just summaries? We need originals for our auditors.
[04:34] Jordan Lee: Trust Center has full PDFs for SOC 2 and scope statements; access is view-only by default. For auditors, we can provide temporary secure downloads or grant auditor access under NDA. We'll note that in the follow-up.
[04:48] Daniel Park: Procurement would like a list of sub-processors and where logs are stored -- are those in the Trust Center as well?
[04:55] Priya Nair: Sub-processor list is in Trust Center and we maintain a contract addendum for major sub-processors. Logs location and retention are documented per deployment type.
[05:05] Evan Morales: Any recent exceptions or ongoing remediation items on the last SOC 2 audit?
[05:10] Priya Nair: No open exceptions impacting security categories -- we had two operational findings around incident runbooks which were closed and validated in Q1 of 2026. We'll include the evidence snapshot.
[05:22] Sofia Ruiz: Network segmentation for Dedicated -- can you confirm that tenant traffic is isolated at the network layer and how you validate?
[05:29] Priya Nair: Tenant isolation for Dedicated uses separate VPCs or VPC segments, combined with firewall policies and strict IAM roles on the orchestration layer. We run regular network scans and penetration tests and include summaries in the compliance pack.
[05:44] Jordan Lee: A quick note for timeline -- if you want Trust Center access this week we'll provision view-only creds; for auditor access it's a two-step with NDA and limited-time tokens.
[05:55] Daniel Park: That works. Procurement will review the SOC 2 PDF and come back. Pricing and SOW next week would be ideal.
[06:03] Evan Morales: For our security team -- can we have a hands-on session around KMS integration? Specifically, how Redwood rotates wrapped keys and how to revoke access programmatically.
[06:13] Priya Nair: Yes, deep dive is good. We'll demo key rotation, the API endpoints for key revoke, and how envelope encryption works. There are a couple of minor UI names that are inconsistent (we call rotate key in console but the API is key-rekey), we'll make sure to point that out.
[06:30] Sofia Ruiz: About the tamper evidence, you mentioned signed manifests -- can we get an example of the signature format? Our tooling expects RFC7515-based JWS metadata.
[06:39] Priya Nair: We use JWS-compatible signatures; I'll include a sample manifest in the follow-up. Good catch on RFC7515.
[06:47] Jordan Lee: Any competitors or alternatives you're evaluating that we should be aware of?
[06:51] Evan Morales: We're looking at ManagedCloudAI as a self-hosted option and Anthropic's enterprise offering. Also Pinecone came up for vector infra but not directly for compliance.
[06:59] Jordan Lee: Helpful to know. We'll include a brief doc on how Redwood's compliance compares focusing on evidence access, KMS options, and dedicated SLAs.
[07:08] Daniel Park: Minor procurement ask -- can we get the auditor's contact info for verification?
[07:12] Priya Nair: We'll redact personal contact in the public docs but we can provide a verified contact point via Kearns & Boyle's auditor portal; will coordinate with legal.
[07:22] Evan Morales: Ok, so recap?
[07:25] Jordan Lee: Recap: 1) We'll give Trust Center view-only access with SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, 2) Priya will produce a SOC2->ISO controls mapping and send a sample audit manifest, 3) schedule a technical deep dive (KMS/HSM) next week, 4) Jordan will send pricing/SOW for Dedicated/Private.
[07:42] Sofia Ruiz: That sounds right. Add: include network diagram and sample audit export.
[07:47] Priya Nair: Noted. Action items I'll add to the follow-up email.
[07:52] Daniel Park: Procurement will review and aim to get back by EOD Friday on next steps.
[07:58] Jordan Lee: Perfect -- we'll target the deep dive for next Wednesday at 15:00 UTC, pending calendar invites.
[08:06] Evan Morales: One last operational Q: do you have SLAs around log ingestion and latency? For our compliance we need logs to be ingested within 5 minutes of event for certain services.
[08:16] Priya Nair: Default ingest latency is sub-60s for admin events in hosted; we can set up streaming exporters for near real-time ingestion to your SIEM. For Dedicated, ingestion SLAs can be part of the contract.
[08:30] Jordan Lee: Great -- thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the Trust Center link and the artifacts.
[08:37] Evan Morales: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
